svg.aria-label: Offline DPO Distribution Shift and Likelihood Displacement vs Online GRPO
svg.text: Post-Training Failure Modes: Offline DPO Likelihood Displacement vs. Online GRPO Verifier Loop
Why unanchored DPO can suppress both chosen and rejected log-probabilities, and how NLL Anchoring / IPO / Online GRPO fix it
A. Likelihood Displacement in Offline DPO (Shared Prefix Trap)
High-Overlap Preference Pair (92% Shared Tokens)
y_w: {"tool": "search_crm", "dealer_id": 402, "status": "ACTIVE"}
y_l: {"tool": "search_crm", "dealer_id": 402, "status": "ALL"}
Shared prefix tokens receive opposing gradients from +grad(y_w) and -grad(y_l)
1. Unanchored Standard DPO Over 3 Epochs:
Epoch 0: log pi(y_w) = -4.2 | log pi(y_l) = -4.5 | Margin = +0.3
Epoch 2: log pi(y_w) = -9.8 | log pi(y_l) = -18.4 | Margin = +8.6
Epoch 3: log pi(y_w) = -14.1 | log pi(y_l) = -29.0 | Margin = +14.9
Margin Delta_w - Delta_l grows (+14.9), so L_DPO -> 0, yet log pi(y_w) dropped
from -4.2 to -14.1! Probability mass leaks to OOD verbose/degenerate text.
Symptom: Validation reward accuracy = 96%, but generation quality collapses!
2. Production Fix: DPO + NLL Anchor (RPO) & IPO Bounded Target
Fix A (NLL Anchor): L = L_DPO - 0.15 * log pi_theta(y_w | x) / |y_w|
Forces positive lower bound on chosen token log-probabilities.
Fix B (IPO Loss): L_IPO = ( (Delta_w - Delta_l) - 1/(2*beta) )^2
Stops pushing margin once target 1/(2*beta) is reached (zero overfitting).
Epoch 3 (Stabilized): log pi(y_w) = -3.6 | log pi(y_l) = -11.2 | Margin = +7.6
Result: Chosen likelihood increases while rejected near-miss is suppressed.
B. Closing the OOD Loop: Iterative Online DPO & Online GRPO
Step 1: On-Policy Group Sampling {y_1, ..., y_G} ~ pi_theta(. | x)
Instead of scoring static stale pairs from pi_SFT, sample G = 8 completions
directly from current policy pi_theta (exposes current OOD blind spots).
vLLM Engine: Continuous batching + PagedAttention prefix sharing across G=8
Step 2: Deterministic Programmatic Verifier / Calibrated RM Scoring
r_i = w_1 * I[SchemaValid(y_i)] + w_2 * I[SQL_AST_Exec(y_i)]
+ w_3 * I[SlotConstraintsMet(y_i)] - w_len * max(0, |y_i| - L_max)
Explicit length penalty prevents verbosity reward hacking!
Zero human annotation latency; immune to sycophancy bias.
Step 3: Production Post-Training Decision Matrix
1. LoRA SFT (r=32, all linear layers, assistant-only loss mask)
First 85-90% of domain gain: teaches tool schemas & domain syntax
2. Offline DPO + NLL Anchor (1-2 epochs on production edit/reject pairs)
Sharpens boundary against near-miss hallucinations; runs on 1-2 GPUs
3. Online GRPO with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR, G=8, k3 KL)
Maximizes multi-step tool DAG & SQL execution accuracy
